mask.name: Mask
mask.guidance: Select channels and models, inspect a preview, then run Mask. Measure consumes the merged arrays; the counts database is not yet a feature table.
mask.documentation_note:
Folder watching uses ``watch_normalization_pool='per_field'`` by default. For a declared static projected acquisition, ``'fixed_map'`` waits for every image in ``conversion_map.csv`` before running the ordinary Mask or Mask/Measure batch with shared percentile normalization and padding. Set ``randomize=False`` and ``batch_size`` greater than one. A timeout never releases an incomplete pool; restart checkpoints bind the declared members, recipes and original input hashes.

Native time-volume Mask accepts a complete fixed Convert map of explicitly identified C/Z/T planes with both ``z_stack`` and ``t_stack`` enabled. Declare TZYX axis order, physical Z spacing and frame interval. Batch ingest and folder watching retain the original planes and build TZYXC archives for 4-D segmentation. This route supports Mask only; it does not enable Measure, tracking or Classify for native time volumes.

convert.guidance: Convert supported microscope formats to a configured TIFF layout while preserving source mappings. Conversion does not generate object measurements.

foreign.guidance: Import external measurements with explicit object/column mappings, or choose Import Images, Format Converter or External Masks. Imported measurements are not a fresh Measure run. external_masks.guidance: Assign corresponding images and existing integer label masks, then create and measure a spaCR project without rerunning segmentation.

queue.guidance: Run the chosen pipeline across plates. Outputs are those of each queued module; retain each plate and its settings separately.

batch.name: Batch Runner
batch.guidance: Validate and execute module jobs in dependency order. Each job writes its own module outputs and log.

distributed_jobs.name: Distributed Jobs
distributed_jobs.guidance: Submit a configured run to a remote execution target and inspect its status and logs. Retrieve the actual module artifacts before downstream analysis.

db_browser.name: Database Browser
db_browser.guidance: Browse selected tables and export rows; table inspection does not rerun image analysis.

run_history.name: Run History
run_history.guidance: Inspect saved run status, settings, outputs and logs; a completed run does not establish biological validity.

report.name: Report
report.guidance: Package recorded results, settings and QC into a shareable report without silently rerunning the analysis.

data_manager.name: Data Manager
data_manager.guidance: Inspect project files and disk usage. Removing derived artifacts invalidates downstream uses of those files; original images must remain recoverable.

pipeline_graph.name: Pipeline Graph
pipeline_graph.guidance: Read recorded artifact dependencies and stale/missing status. The graph describes provenance and does not regenerate missing artifacts.

qc_dashboard.name: QC
qc_dashboard.guidance: Inspect stored segmentation, unit, leakage and plate-effect checks. Open its nested viewers for detailed inspection.

lineage.name: Lineage
lineage.guidance: Inspect recorded cell/nucleus/pathogen/organelle containment links; this is object containment, not time-series lineage inference.

experiment_design.name: Experiment Design
experiment_design.guidance: Enter conditions, controls, replicates and plate constraints, then export the experimental layout before acquisition.

layer_viewer.name: Layer Viewer
layer_viewer.guidance: Inspect aligned image, label and point/ROI layers for the selected field.

power.name: Power / Design
power.guidance: Estimate sampling needs from chosen effect sizes and variability; pilot measurements are optional evidence for assumptions.

run_compare.name: Run Compare
run_compare.guidance: Compare compatible saved settings, counts and hit lists without treating changed input data as a controlled model comparison.

tabulate.name: Tabulate
tabulate.guidance: Choose grouping variables and measurement columns, then inspect pivot tables and groupwise sample sizes.

dose_response.name: Dose–Response
dose_response.guidance: Supply dose and response columns, controls and units before curve fitting; this route does not require sequencing.

project_browser.name: Project Browser
project_browser.guidance: Locate projects and inspect their stage, last run, disk use and stale outputs.

outliers.name: Outliers
outliers.guidance: Review robust object/well outlier scores and the selected exclusion rule before carrying filtered data into analysis.

embeddings.name: Embeddings
embeddings.guidance: Encode object images with a chosen model and channel policy. Retain object identities and encoder provenance when supplying the features to downstream exploration.
embeddings.documentation_note: With alpha features enabled, **Save for Similar crops** stores the full embedding matrix in the measurements database that supplied the loaded objects. It requires the original database object identities and verified encoder weights. Annotate can then search those stored vectors with compatible model, channel and preprocessing identities. Folder-loaded crops use the standalone Python example to save matrices; they cannot use the database save action.

control_chart.name: Control Charts
control_chart.guidance: Compare designated controls across plates and inspect drift; the definition of a control comes from the experiment.

train_compare.name: Training Runs
train_compare.guidance: Compare saved training histories, metrics and settings from compatible model runs.

align.name: Align & Stitch
align.guidance: Inspect tile geometry, overlap and channel mapping, then save the mosaic with coordinate records. OPS also needs the original cycle/site identities.

make_masks.name: Make Masks
make_masks.guidance: Curate image/mask pairs for segmentation training, or use Organize for Measure to merge images and their masks into arrays Measure reads. Saving a mask does not train a classifier.

plate_view.name: Plate Viewer
plate_view.guidance: Aggregate the selected measurement by well and inspect plate patterns and controls.

umap.name: Image UMAP
umap.guidance: Project measured features or supplied encoder features and inspect representative crops. A cluster is a candidate grouping, not a validated phenotype. Use the lasso and annotation controls to write reviewed selections to an annotation column in the matching measurement database. A geometric selection alone does not establish a biological phenotype.

profiler.name: Prediction Profiler
profiler.guidance: Inspect how a fitted model responds as an input feature changes; predictions do not establish causal effects.

graph_builder.name: Graph Builder
graph_builder.guidance: Load a table or use Merge tables to combine compatible measurements. For converted images, use Merge original filenames to recover names from a conversion map. Use Annotate conditions to assign a named column with metadata regex rules or dragged rows; save an annotated SQLite table or export CSV with its rules. Choose variables, groups and plotting settings, then export the figure with its analysis context.

investigate_hit.name: Investigate Hit
investigate_hit.guidance: Link a regression hit to candidate objects and quantitative well-level evidence. This does not independently validate the hit.

gate_editor.name: Gate Editor
gate_editor.guidance: Load a table or use Merge tables to create a working set with validated keys and aggregation. Define threshold or polygon gates on actual feature/coordinate columns, then apply the saved gate to compatible objects. Use Annotate to write the displayed gates to an annotation column; review the selected objects and choose binary or multiclass labels.

feature_dict.name: Feature Dictionary
feature_dict.guidance: Look up feature definitions and units before choosing measurement columns.

trellis.name: Small Multiples
trellis.guidance: Compare groups in small-multiple plots with explicit shared or independent axes.

analyze_plaques.name: Plaque Assay

recruitment.name: Recruitment
recruitment.guidance: Use compartment intensity measurements and matching host/pathogen identities to compute recruitment ratios.

invasion.name: Invasion Assay
invasion.guidance: Use the required two-colour differential-staining measurements and stain-baseline controls to distinguish attachment from invasion.

replication.name: Replication Assay
replication.guidance: Count parasites using explicit vacuole identity and compare condition distributions; host identity alone does not define a vacuole.

train_cellpose.name: Cellpose Workbench
train_cellpose.guidance: Open Cellpose Workbench inside Make Masks and train from verified image/mask pairs. Evaluate on separate fields before selecting the checkpoint in Mask.

cellpose_all.name: Mask folder
cellpose_all.guidance: Apply the selected segmentation model to the open image folder through Make Masks; inspect saved labels before measuring them.

model_compare.name: Model Compare
model_compare.guidance: Compare model masks on identical fields. Without independent reference labels, agreement does not measure segmentation accuracy.

model_zoo.name: Model Zoo
model_zoo.guidance: Inspect model provenance and download/install compatible checkpoints or backends. A listed backend is not itself a checkpoint file.

curate.name: Curate
curate.guidance: Correct labels and track assignments while retaining a record of the edits.

napari_bridge.name: Napari Bridge
napari_bridge.guidance: Send the matching image/labels to napari and import the revised labels back with field identity preserved.

import_images.name: Import Images
import_images.guidance: Review field identities, image channels and optional external masks before writing a separate project. Image-only imports still need segmentation before measurement.

barcode_qc.name: Barcode QC
barcode_qc.guidance: Inspect mapping depth, coverage, collisions and positional effects before guide-count filtering.

image_scatter.name: Image Scatter
image_scatter.guidance: Plot selected measurement columns with object-crop inspection.

pca.name: PCA
pca.guidance: Inspect principal components and feature loadings for the selected measured objects.

volcano_explorer.name: Volcano Explorer
volcano_explorer.guidance: Open a saved regression result and inspect effect sizes, adjusted significance and individual hit records.

hit_list.name: Hit List
hit_list.guidance: Filter and rank saved hits with their effects, FDR and guide agreement.

methods_export.name: Methods & Results
methods_export.guidance: Draft methods/results text from recorded settings and results; review every claim before publication.

regression_diagnostics.name: Diagnostics
regression_diagnostics.guidance: Inspect the diagnostic panels saved by the chosen regression run; distinguish missing diagnostics from passed assumptions.

illumination.name: Illumination

anndata_export.name: AnnData Export
anndata_export.guidance: Export an AnnData .h5ad file with object metadata and measured features for downstream single-cell analysis.

motility.name: Motility Assay
motility.guidance: Inspect track speed and infection-related measurements with an explicit frame interval and pixel calibration.

timelapse.name: Timelapse

timelapse.documentation_note: Lineage exports retain generation times in frames and add ``generation_time_hours`` with calibrated summary statistics. Supply a positive ``frame_interval_s`` or complete, increasing ``time_s`` values in the tracks table. If both are present, they must agree; irregular timestamps are supported without a fixed interval. Missing calibration and incomplete cell cycles have no generation time in hours. explain_cv.name: Explain CV Model

parameter_sweep.name: Parameter Sweep
parameter_sweep.guidance: Run explicitly selected regression settings and compare their diagnostics. Keep the input data and evaluation question fixed.

toxoplasma.name: Toxoplasma
toxoplasma.guidance: Open the organism guide from Home, inspect the compartment diagram, then select Plaque Assay, Recruitment, Invasion Assay or Replication Assay. The four Coming soon tiles describe proposals and cannot run. The guide itself does not analyse a project or produce a measurement table.

endodyogeny.name: Endodyogeny size proxy
endodyogeny.guidance: Read measured compartment areas, annotate conditions and bin area ** 1.5 into log2 size doublings. Defaults aggregate pathogen area per host cell, not per vacuole: multiple vacuoles in one cell are combined. This is an area-derived size proxy, not measured volume or a parasite count. Use Replication Assay with explicit vacuole identity for parasites-per-vacuole counts. Configure compartment, area filters, calibration, conditions and grouping before calling the API; saving is optional.

cellpose_masks.name: Direct Cellpose mask generation
cellpose_masks.guidance: Run a stock or custom Cellpose model on TIFF fields through the Python API. Despite its historical identify_masks_finetune name, this function performs inference, not training. Review normalization, channels, resizing and model parameters; masks are written only when save is enabled. Import compatible image/mask pairs through External Masks before Measure, or curate the pairs before training. This call does not build a Measure-ready merged project.

simulation.name: Pooled-screen simulation sweep
simulation.guidance: Use the Python sweep API to explore stated screen-design assumptions. It expands combinations, runs simulations in a process pool and writes synthetic summary statistics; it returns None. Set a small explicit max_workers value and a bounded parameter grid before running. The output does not replace measurements or barcode counts for experimental Regression. Use the findings as planning evidence, with their assumptions recorded. Review the synthetic summaries when choosing planning assumptions; transfer those assumptions manually into Power / Design or Experiment Design. Neither tool imports this simulation database, and neither exports the simulation settings grid.

host_pathogen.name: Host–Pathogen Analysis
host_pathogen.guidance: Measure whole vacuoles and host reference compartments, keeping uninfected host cells for the infection denominator. Select marker channels and control-calibrated ratio thresholds. Optionally count individually segmented parasites from explicit vacuole links or a measured count column. Review vacuole, host and well tables, joint marker states, replication distributions and unmatched parasite links; unknown measurements remain unknown.

spatial_masks.name: Spatial Mask Generation
spatial_masks.guidance: Alpha. Segment a whole Xenium morphology or Visium HD H&E slide in overlapping windows; each window is written to merged/ with its masks, the layout Measure reads, and the windows' places on the slide go to measurements.db for Spatial Map Barcodes. In the GUI it is the Spatial switch in Mask Generation's actions row, shown only with Show alpha features on.

spatial_map.name: Spatial Map Barcodes
spatial_map.guidance: Alpha. Count every Xenium transcript or Visium HD bin into the cell or nucleus it falls in, using the fields Spatial Mask Generation wrote; per-object expression tables and infection calls from pathogen genes go into measurements.db keyed like Measure's. In the GUI it is the Spatial switch in Map Barcodes' actions row, shown only with Show alpha features on.

pooled_screen.title: A pooled spaCR screen

steps.action: Start on Home and open Mask. Load the example data, check channels and segmentation, then run.
Return Home and open Map Barcodes for the matching sequencing reads and references.

If segmentation already exists, import the matching images and external masks into a spaCR project and inspect the resulting object identities. Skip segmentation and proceed to Measure when its required arrays are present.
Open Measure with the Mask project and create measurements and object crops.
Open Annotate, inspect representative objects and save phenotype labels.

Load a table or use Merge tables to create a working set with validated keys and aggregation. Define threshold or polygon gates on actual feature/coordinate columns, then apply the saved gate to compatible objects. Use Annotate to write the displayed gates to an annotation column; review the selected objects and choose binary or multiclass labels.

Project measured features or supplied encoder features and inspect representative crops. A cluster is a candidate grouping, not a validated phenotype. Use the lasso and annotation controls to write reviewed selections to an annotation column in the matching measurement database. A geometric selection alone does not establish a biological phenotype.
Open Classify, choose images or measured features, and inspect held-out predictions.
Open Regression with compatible phenotype scores and per-well guide counts; inspect hits and diagnostics.

pooled_screen.description: Combine image-derived phenotypes with guide abundance to rank perturbations. Segment and measure images, create reviewed labels with Annotate, Gate Editor or Image UMAP, and train and validate a classifier. Map the matching sequencing reads on an independent branch. Join compatible phenotype scores and guide counts by experimental identity for Regression. Annotation and segmentation routes are alternatives, not requirements to run every branch.

inputs.title: FASTQ: R1/R2, R1 only or R2 only
inputs.description: Supply gzipped FASTQ files and the barcode reference CSVs. Use paired mode for R1/R2. For single-end reads, choose single mode and set single_direction to R1 or R2 to match the files and extraction orientation.

high_content.title: High-content image analysis

If segmentation already exists, import the matching images and external masks into a spaCR project and inspect the resulting object identities. Skip segmentation and proceed to Measure when its required arrays are present.
Open Measure on the resulting project and quantify objects.
Open Image UMAP to explore measured phenotypes and inspect crops.
Open Gate Editor to define an explicit population filter.
Open Graph Builder to compare the chosen measurements and groups.

high_content.description: Quantify an imaging experiment without sequencing. Start with microscopy images or import existing masks with their source images, measure the objects, then explore embeddings, define gated populations or build figures. These downstream branches answer different questions and can be used independently.

Inside Make Masks open Cellpose Workbench, choose Train and use the curated pairs.
Return Home, open Mask and select the trained checkpoint; verify separate fields before a full run.

segmentation_training.description: Build a segmentation model from curated image and integer-mask pairs. Correct representative images in Make Masks, train in Cellpose Workbench, and select the resulting checkpoint in Mask. Evaluate independent fields before processing the full experiment; training images are not a held-out accuracy test.

parasite_assay.title: Toxoplasma and parasite imaging assays

steps.action: Start on Home with Mask and configure the host, parasite and required compartment masks.

If segmentation already exists, import the matching images and external masks into a spaCR project and inspect the resulting object identities. Skip segmentation and proceed to Measure when its required arrays are present.
Open Measure and collect the compartment or staining measurements needed by your assay.
For a recruitment question, open Recruitment and inspect compartment intensity ratios.

Measure whole vacuoles and host reference compartments, keeping uninfected host cells for the infection denominator. Select marker channels and control-calibrated ratio thresholds. Optionally count individually segmented parasites from explicit vacuole links or a measured count column. Review vacuole, host and well tables, joint marker states, replication distributions and unmatched parasite links; unknown measurements remain unknown.
Use the required two-colour differential-staining measurements and stain-baseline controls to distinguish attachment from invasion.
Count parasites using explicit vacuole identity and compare condition distributions; host identity alone does not define a vacuole.

78_spacr_screens.title: spaCR screens
78_spacr_screens.description: Follow a pooled image-based screen from Home through image measurements, phenotype classification, barcode counts and regression.
78_spacr_screens.introduction: A pooled screen tells its story twice, once in images and once in sequencing reads, and spaCR brings the two together at the end. On the image side, Mask and Measure turn your microscope fields into measured cells, and Annotate and Classify turn those cells into phenotype scores. On the sequencing side, Map Barcodes turns reads into guide counts. Regression joins the two by plate and well. Join wherever your results begin.
78_spacr_screens.conclusion: So a pooled screen runs as two streams that meet in Regression. Before you open it, check that the plate and well identifiers match across your scores, guide counts and plate layout, and keep the annotation column, classifier settings and barcode references with the run. The linked module lessons walk through each step, or choose the pooled-screen walkthrough on Home.

scenes.mask: Everything starts with your microscope images. Open Mask from Home, choose the channels and a segmentation model, and check the preview before you run it. Mask finds the objects in every field and saves each field as a merged array, the image channels stacked with their label masks. Those merged arrays are what Measure opens next. The small counts database Mask leaves behind is only a tally, not yet a feature table.
scenes.measure: Next, open Measure from Home and point it at the same project, with the image and mask channel indices set correctly. Measure reads each merged array, images and label planes together, and writes every cell, nucleus or parasite as a row in measurements.db. Turn on crop saving and it also cuts a small PNG around each object, indexed in png_list. From here the story forks. Annotate shows those crops so you can label examples, and Classify learns from either the crops or the measured features, so keep object identities stable.
scenes.annotate: Before a classifier can learn anything, it needs examples. Open Annotate from Home and it shows you the object crops Measure saved or streams. Click through representative cells and label them. Each label is written to an annotation column in the png_list table, tied to that object's identity. Use a separate column for each question, and set some labelled objects aside for evaluation. That annotation column is what Classify trains on next.
scenes.classify_merged: Open Classify from Home, and here your labels become scores. Classify has two families, and your data picks between them. Computer Vision learns from the object crops themselves, while Tabular Machine Learning learns from the measured feature columns. Either way, it trains on the labels you made in Annotate, checks itself on the objects you held out, and saves the trained model, an evaluation bundle and the scores, as CSV files and, when merged, in png_list. Pick the CV or ML score column you mean to test, keep plate and well identity intact, and carry it into Regression.
scenes.map_barcodes: While the images go one way, the sequencing reads go another. Open Map Barcodes from Home, give it your FASTQ files and the barcode references that encode your screen, and it counts which guides turned up in each well. Check the mapped counts and barcode QC before you trust them. The unique_combinations.csv it writes is the guide-count table Regression pairs with your phenotype scores, well by well.
scenes.regression: This is where the two halves of the screen meet. Open Regression from Home and give it both: the phenotype scores from Classify and the guide counts from Map Barcodes. Regression matches them on plate and well, so those keys have to agree in both files. Choose the response column and your controls, run the fit, and open the diagnostics before you believe any hit. If your barcodes were read optically with OPS instead, join and aggregate the decoded objects to your phenotype and guide data first; OPS does not hand over a ready-made count table. Regression can also model a directly measured response. It writes a results folder of coefficients, hit tables, settings and diagnostic figures.

79_module_inputs_outputs.title: Module inputs and outputs
79_module_inputs_outputs.description: Find every current module's input data, saved outputs, upstream producers and downstream consumers, including tools nested inside a Home module.
79_module_inputs_outputs.introduction: Think of this lesson as a map of where each file goes. Every chapter is one module: how to open it, what it reads, what it writes and which module picks that output up next. Start from the files you have or the result you need, and follow the handoffs from there. Keep object, plate and well identifiers with your data as it travels.
79_module_inputs_outputs.conclusion: When you know your next task, jump to its chapter and open the linked module lesson for its controls and example data. Keep every output beside the settings that made it. The module pages and the Python API describe the same files, tables and identifiers when you connect steps in your own analysis.

80_image_analysis_pathways.title: Image analysis modules and how they relate
80_image_analysis_pathways.description: Choose an image-analysis route through segmentation, measurement, annotation, classification, projections, gates, image registration, quality control and assays.
80_image_analysis_pathways.introduction: The image-analysis modules usually run in this order. Mask segments objects in the raw images and writes merged image arrays and label masks. To correct masks by hand or import existing masks, use Make Masks. Measure reads the merged arrays and masks, writes per-object measurements to a database and can also save a PNG crop of each object. Classification, image exploration, gating and the assay modules start from those measurements and crops. When tiles must share one coordinate system, build a mosaic in Align & Stitch first.
80_image_analysis_pathways.conclusion: Most image analyses run Mask, then Measure, then one downstream module. To train a segmentation model, curate image-mask pairs in Make Masks, train them in Cellpose Workbench and load the saved model in Mask. A module can start later in the sequence when its inputs already exist. Keep channel identities, units and object keys with each result so later modules can match them.

scenes.mask: Raw microscope images begin in Mask. Open it from Home, choose the channels and segmentation models, and check the preview before you run. Mask writes each field as a merged array, the image channels and their integer label planes together, and that merged array is what Measure reads next. Mask also keeps a small counts database, but that is a tally, not a feature table.
scenes.make_masks: Sometimes masks need a human hand. Open Make Masks from Home to correct them field by field. What you save here can go two ways. To train segmentation, curate image and mask pairs and keep them side by side as training fields. To measure, use Organize for Measure, which moves each image and its masks into channel folders and merges them into the arrays Measure reads; a standalone mask is not a merged array. Plaque masks drawn here can also feed the Plaque Assay with their matching source images. Saving a mask does not train a classifier.
scenes.measure: Measure is the hub of this whole map. Open it from Home and point it at the project Mask built, with the image and mask channel indices set correctly; masks paired in Make Masks arrive here too. Measure reads the images and label planes together and writes every cell, nucleus or parasite as a row in measurements.db. Turn on crop saving if you want a PNG of each object, and keep the database with its source project if you stream crops instead. Almost everything else starts from these rows. Annotate and Classify use the measurements and crops to learn phenotypes. Image UMAP projects them so you can look for groupings, and Embeddings encodes the crops with a model, recording the encoder and channel policy. Gate Editor sets thresholds on the real measured features, in their real units, and QC shows which checks exist and which are missing. The Toxoplasma assays pick up here as well: Recruitment needs the right compartment intensities, the Invasion Assay needs two-colour stain measurements with baseline controls, and the Replication Assay needs explicit parasite-to-vacuole links. Host–Pathogen Analysis wants whole-vacuole masks and host reference intensities, with the uninfected cells kept in. And the Endodyogeny size proxy reads the measured project from Python, once you have checked host-cell aggregation and area units; the Mask counts database alone is not enough.
scenes.annotate: With measurements in hand, Annotate is where you teach by example. Open it from Home and it shows the object crops Measure saved or streams from the project. Label representative objects; each label goes into an annotation column of the png_list table, tied to that object's identity. You don't have to start from nothing: gates saved in Gate Editor can propose candidate labels for you to review. Use a separate column for each question, keep training and evaluation objects apart, and that column is what Classify trains on next.
scenes.classify_merged: Open Classify from Home to turn labels into predictions. It has two families, and your data decides between them. Computer Vision learns from object crops, saved or streamed by Measure; Tabular Machine Learning learns from the measured feature columns. The labels can come from three places. Most often they come from Annotate. Gate Editor can write reviewed gate selections to an annotation column, and Image UMAP can do the same with reviewed lasso selections; either way, select that same column and object population here. An embedding cluster is not ground truth, so inspect the crops, validate the labels and keep validation objects apart from training. Classify then saves its scores, the trained model and an evaluation bundle of held-out predictions. In a screen, pick the CV or ML score column you mean and carry it, plate and well identity intact, into Regression.
scenes.umap: Image UMAP is for looking before you label. Open it from Home and it projects the measured features from Measure, or encoder features from Embeddings with matching object IDs, into a map where similar objects sit close together. Open representative crops to see what a region really holds. A cluster is only a candidate grouping, not a validated phenotype. When a region does look meaningful, draw a lasso around it, review what you caught, and write the selection to an annotation column in the matching measurement database. Classify can then train on that column. The projection can also go to Gate Editor, if you would rather define the selection there with the matching coordinate and feature columns. Not every GUI route saves encoder features for you, and a shape on a plot alone does not establish a biological phenotype.
scenes.gate_editor: Gate Editor lets you choose objects by rule rather than by eye. Open it from Home and draw threshold or polygon gates on real columns: measured features from Measure, in their actual units, or the coordinates of an Image UMAP projection. Save a gate and you can apply it again to any compatible objects. Its Annotate button writes the displayed gates to an annotation column, once you have reviewed the selected objects and chosen binary or multiclass labels. Saved gates can also propose candidate labels inside Annotate. Then select that same column and object population in Classify, keeping validation objects separate from the training labels.
scenes.align: Some analyses need tiles stitched into one picture first. Open Align & Stitch from Home, check the tile geometry, overlap and channel mapping, and save the mosaic with its coordinate records. For OPS, keep the original cycle and site identities as well.
scenes.analyze_plaques: Now the Toxoplasma assays. Open Toxoplasma from Home and choose Plaque Assay. This one skips Measure: it reads plaque images, or masks you already have, and runs the configured plaque model. Masks from Make Masks work here if they are plaque masks with matching source images; cell masks are not plaque labels. It saves plaque results and masks, and the plaque example lesson shows a full run.
scenes.recruitment: Recruitment asks how much of a marker gathers at the parasite. Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose Recruitment. It reads compartment intensities from Measure, with matching host and pathogen identities, and computes recruitment ratios that keep each well and condition.
scenes.host_pathogen: Host–Pathogen Analysis looks at infection from both sides. Open Toxoplasma from Home, then choose it. It reads measurements from Measure that include whole vacuoles, host reference compartments and the uninfected host cells, which form the infection denominator. Select the marker channels and set ratio thresholds calibrated on your controls. If you segmented individual parasites, it can count them per vacuole from explicit links or a measured count column. You then get vacuole, host and well tables, joint marker states, replication distributions and any parasite links it could not match. Unknown measurements stay unknown, and host identity alone never defines a vacuole.
scenes.invasion: To tell parasites that merely attached from those that got inside, open Toxoplasma from Home and choose Invasion Assay. It relies on two-colour differential-staining measurements from Measure, together with stain-baseline controls, and saves assay results with each well and condition intact.
scenes.replication: The Replication Assay, also under Toxoplasma on Home, counts parasites in each vacuole and compares those distributions between conditions. It reads objects from Measure, but it needs explicit parasite-to-vacuole identities; host identity alone does not define a vacuole.
scenes.qc_dashboard: Any time after Measure, open QC from Home to check your work. It reads the stored checks for segmentation, units, leakage and plate effects, and its nested viewers let you look closer. A missing check is not a passing one. QC saves its results with exportable figures and tables.
scenes.embeddings: Embeddings describes objects by what a model sees rather than by hand-picked features. Open it from Home, choose a model and a channel policy, and it encodes the object crops Measure produced into one feature vector per object. Record the object identities, the encoder and the channel policy with those features, because Image UMAP needs a feature table with matching object IDs, and not every route saves one for you.
scenes.endodyogeny: Two tools in this map live only in Python. The first is the endodyogeny size proxy, spacr.submodules.analyze_endodyogeny; it has no Home tile or menu entry. It reads measured compartment areas from your Measure projects, labels them by condition, and bins area to the power of one and a half into log2 size doublings. By default it sums pathogen area per host cell, not per vacuole, so several vacuoles in one cell are combined. That makes it an area-derived size proxy, not a measured volume or a parasite count; for parasites per vacuole, use the Replication Assay. Set the compartment, area filters, calibration, conditions and grouping before you call it, and check aggregation and area units before reading the bins. The Mask counts database alone is not enough.
scenes.cellpose_masks: The second is direct Cellpose mask generation, spacr.spacr_cellpose.identify_masks_finetune, again with no Home tile or menu entry. Despite that name, it runs inference, not training: it applies a stock or custom Cellpose model to the TIFF fields in a folder. Check normalization, channels, resizing and model settings first, and enable saving, because masks are written only when save is on. What you get are label TIFFs, not a Measure-ready project. To carry on, import the image and mask pairs through External Masks before Measure, or curate them for training.

81_sequencing_pathways.title: Sequencing modules and how they relate
81_sequencing_pathways.description: Connect sequencing and optical barcode workflows to phenotype scores, regression, experiment planning, power estimates, dose-response analysis and run comparison.
81_sequencing_pathways.introduction: Sequencing is how a pooled screen learns which guide sits in which well or cell, and spaCR reads it two ways. Reads from a sequencer go into Map Barcodes. Barcodes imaged cycle by cycle go into OPS, which lives inside Mask. Either way, the barcode identities end up beside your phenotypes in Regression. Around that core sit the planning tools, Experiment Design and Power, for before you acquire, and Dose–Response and Run Compare for your results.
81_sequencing_pathways.conclusion: So the barcode side of a screen always ends the same way: identities joined to phenotypes by plate and well. Keep barcode references and plate layouts with your count tables, and for an optical screen, join the decoded objects to their phenotypes and aggregate them before Regression. The linked module lessons show the settings and outputs for each step.

scenes.map_barcodes: Start with the sequencing reads. Open Map Barcodes from Home and give it your FASTQ files, single-end or paired, with the barcode reference tables that encode your experiment. Map Barcodes matches each read to its barcodes and counts the guides in every well, saving unique_combinations.csv and annotated_reads.h5 in its run folder. Before you trust those counts, open them in Barcode QC. Once they pass, they are the guide counts Regression pairs with phenotype scores, on the same plate and well keys.
scenes.barcode_qc: Barcode QC lives inside Map Barcodes, so open Map Barcodes from Home and choose it there. It reads the guide counts you just made and shows mapping depth, coverage, barcode collisions and positional effects. It saves the QC results with exportable figures and tables, so you can decide which guides to filter before going further.
scenes.ops: Optical screens take a different road. Open Mask from Home, then choose OPS. Instead of reads, OPS takes the images from each sequencing cycle, aligns them to the phenotype images and decodes a barcode for every nucleus. The results land in the OPS measurements.db, with tables for geometry, phenotype alignment, nuclei and barcodes. That database is not a FASTQ count table, though. To use it in Regression, first join and aggregate the decoded identities with your phenotype data, so each object or well carries both.
scenes.regression: Whichever way you sequenced, barcodes meet phenotypes in Regression. Open it from Home. For a pooled screen, it takes phenotype scores from Classify and guide counts from Map Barcodes. For an optical screen, it takes the decoded OPS objects once you have joined and aggregated them yourself; that is not a direct file handoff. It can also model a directly measured response. In every case, plate and well identifiers must agree across the inputs. Choose the response and the controls, run the fit, and read the diagnostics before you call anything a hit. The results folder it writes, with coefficients, hit tables, settings and figures, is what Run Compare opens when you want to line this run up against another.
scenes.power: Now step back to before the experiment. Open Power / Design from Home to estimate how much sampling you need to see an effect, based on the effect sizes and variability you choose. Pilot measurements can support those assumptions, but they are optional. The layout from Experiment Design feeds these estimates, and the estimates in turn may send you back to revise that design.
scenes.experiment_design: Open Experiment Design from Home to lay out the plates before you acquire anything. Enter the conditions, controls, replicates and plate constraints, with your power estimates in mind, and export the experimental layout. That layout travels far. Power / Design uses it to set sampling assumptions, and later, once the experiment is acquired and measured, Dose–Response uses its dose and condition identities, so keep them unchanged all the way through.
scenes.dose_response: Dose–Response answers how much, not which guide, so it needs no sequencing at all. Open it from Home and bring your measured responses with the dose and condition identities from Experiment Design. Set the dose and response columns, controls and units, then fit the curves. It saves assay results with figures and tables to export.
scenes.run_compare: Once you have more than one analysis, open Run Compare from Home. It reads your saved run records and Regression results and sets their settings, counts and hit lists side by side. If the input data changed between runs, the differences are not a controlled model comparison, so read them with that in mind.
scenes.simulation: One more planning tool lives only in Python: the pooled-screen simulation sweep, spacr.sim.run_multiple_simulations, with no Home tile or menu entry. You give it a settings dictionary of assumptions, such as screen size, occupancy, classifier accuracy and sequencing. It expands every combination, simulates each in a process pool and appends synthetic summary rows to simulations.db; the call itself returns None. Keep the parameter grid small and set max_workers explicitly before you run it. What comes out is planning evidence, not data, and it cannot stand in for measurements or barcode counts in Regression. Read the summaries, record your assumptions, and carry them by hand into Power / Design or Experiment Design, since neither tool imports the simulation database.

small_images.explanation: Image counts are descriptive, not a validity threshold. Collections with fewer than ten images are supported; inspect representative fields.

tiff_yokogawa.label: TIFF with Yokogawa metadata
tiff_yokogawa.explanation: Use the CellVoyager filename convention; verify plate, well, field and channel identities before analysis.

tiff_other.label: TIFF with other metadata
tiff_other.explanation: Choose the actual filename convention or a custom named-group expression. Test it on representative files.

other_yokogawa.label: Other images with Yokogawa metadata
other_yokogawa.explanation: Choose a supported image container. Import or convert it before a tool that requires organized TIFFs.

other_metadata.label: Other images with other metadata
other_metadata.explanation: Select the actual image container and filename convention. Optional vendor readers must be installed; inspect their axes before conversion.

pdf.label: Images on a PDF
pdf.explanation: Use Plaque Assay for scanned monolayers. Inspect page extraction, scale, well boundaries and plaque masks; a PDF is not a general microscopy input.

plate_images.label: Many images, high content (>50)
plate_images.explanation: Preserve plate, well, field, channel, time and Z identities. The image count does not select a scientific model.

tiff_yokogawa.label: TIFF with Yokogawa metadata
tiff_yokogawa.explanation: Use the CellVoyager filename convention; verify plate, well, field and channel identities before analysis.

tiff_other.label: TIFF with other metadata
tiff_other.explanation: Choose the actual filename convention or a custom named-group expression. Test it on representative files.

other_yokogawa.label: Other images with Yokogawa metadata
other_yokogawa.explanation: Choose a supported image container. Import or convert it before a tool that requires organized TIFFs.

other_metadata.label: Other images with other metadata
other_metadata.explanation: Select the actual image container and filename convention. Optional vendor readers must be installed; inspect their axes before conversion.

pdf.label: Images on a PDF
pdf.explanation: Use Plaque Assay for scanned monolayers. Inspect page extraction, scale, well boundaries and plaque masks; a PDF is not a general microscopy input.

sequencing.label: Sequencing data
sequencing.explanation: Choose the actual read format and pairing. The current barcode mapper requires gzip-compressed FASTQ with recognized mate filenames and matching barcode references.

fastq_gz.label: Gzip-compressed FASTQ (.fastq.gz)
fastq_gz.explanation: The current folder reader groups <sample>_R1… / _R2… and <run>_1 / _2 names. Verify mates and barcode references; machine names do not set decoding parameters.

other.label: Other or unknown read format
other.explanation: Convert and validate reads before Map Barcodes. Additional formats, mixed pairing and machine-specific decoding require the separate sequencing capability work in N740.

features.label: Feature set
features.explanation: Choose the table source and whether matching object images are available. Table-only analyses do not require image crops; image-dependent tools need verified image/object provenance.

database_crops.label: spaCR-compatible database with crops
database_crops.explanation: Retain the measurement database, object identities and matching saved or streamable object images.

database.label: spaCR-compatible database without crops
database.explanation: Use table-based analyses. Image-dependent annotation or classification requires separately verified source images and masks.

external_database.label: Other database
external_database.explanation: Validate table schemas, keys and numeric columns. Import maps external object and image identities; no image provenance is inferred from a numeric table.

csv.label: Other CSV/TSV feature table
csv.explanation: Inspect delimiter, header, identity and numeric columns. Import image/object provenance separately when required.

tif.label: TIFF (.tif)
tif.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

tiff.label: TIFF (.tiff)
tiff.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

png.label: PNG
png.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

jpg.label: JPEG (.jpg)
jpg.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

jpeg.label: JPEG (.jpeg)
jpeg.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

bmp.label: BMP
bmp.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

nd2.label: Nikon ND2 (optional reader)
nd2.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

czi.label: Zeiss CZI (optional reader)
czi.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

lif.label: Leica LIF (optional reader)
lif.explanation: Inspect a representative file and verify reader availability and axes before conversion.

screen.label: spaCR / pooled screen
screen.explanation: Regression requires compatible phenotype responses and mapped guide counts with matching plate and well identities.

drug.label: Drug screen
drug.explanation: Dose–Response needs explicit concentration, treatment, control and replicate metadata. Drug-screen Regression compatibility remains separate work in N741.

other.label: Other experiment / organism
other.explanation: Select the organism and use only its registered existing analysis routes. A proposed assay without an implementation is not an available module.

paired.label: Paired-end reads
paired.explanation: Both recognized mates must be present; paired barcode extraction uses their consensus.

single.label: Single-end reads
single.explanation: Choose the mate orientation used by the barcode pattern and references.

mixed.label: Paired and unpaired reads together
mixed.explanation: The current mapper runs one pairing mode at a time. Separate validated runs are required; mixed-input runtime support belongs to N740.

illumina.label: Illumina-style read naming
illumina.explanation: Verify the actual read orientations and reference sequences; the machine name does not establish a barcode layout.

other.label: Other / unknown sequencer
other.explanation: Only the documented FASTQ and filename contract is currently accepted. Do not infer a machine or scientific decoding parameters.

mapped.label: Barcodes already mapped
mapped.explanation: Supply compatible guide-count and phenotype tables with matched experimental identities.

unmapped.label: Barcodes not mapped
unmapped.explanation: Map the sequencing reads first; a feature table alone cannot produce barcode counts.

requirements.sequencing: Additional sequence formats and mixed-input or machine-specific handling require N740; this protocol does not add a reader.
requirements.drug: Drug-screen Regression compatibility requires N741; no drug model or guide/barcode semantics are invented here.

overview.guidance: Inspect plate, well and field identities, compare image channels, arrange captured views on a canvas and export PDFs or whole-image measurements. Display normalization does not change stored image intensities.
overview.name: Overview

3d.guidance: Open the existing three-dimensional Mask route. Verify Z/channel axes, spacing and a compatible segmentation model before a preview; it is not a conversion of ordinary two-dimensional measurements.
3d.name: 3D

parascape.guidance: Explore the installed Toxoplasma knowledge map in its separate alpha application. Availability follows the normal alpha preferences; reference locations are not measured protein abundances.
parascape.name: ParaScape
